vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: obsidian
Version: 1.0.0

The skill is classified as suspicious due to its reliance on installing a third-party command-line tool (`obsidian-cli`) from a custom Homebrew tap (`yakitrak/yakitrak`) as specified in `SKILL.md`. This introduces a supply chain risk, as the integrity of the `obsidian-cli` tool depends on the `yakitrak` maintainer. Additionally, `SKILL.md` explicitly instructs the AI agent to read a local configuration file (`~/Library/Application Support/obsidian/obsidian.json`), which, while necessary for the stated purpose, represents a direct instruction for file system access, a high-risk capability. There is no clear evidence of intentional malicious behavior like data exfiltration or persistence.

llm.summary: This skill is a straightforward Obsidian helper, with a visible third-party CLI install that users should trust-check before use.

dimensions.detail: The skill reads the Obsidian vault registry and works within user vault files; this is proportionate for Obsidian automation and it explicitly warns not to guess vaults or usually touch .obsidian configuration.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact declares installation of obsidian-cli from the third-party Homebrew tap yakitrak/yakitrak without a pinned version or digest, creating a supply-chain trust consideration, but the install is disclosed and purpose-aligned.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions are scoped to locating Obsidian vaults, using obsidian-cli, and editing Markdown notes; no hidden role changes, prompt hijacking, unrelated data collection, or automatic execution instructions were found.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, background services, privilege escalation, credential harvesting, or tool wrapping were found; the only persistent change described is setting obsidian-cli's default vault when the user chooses to do so.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's capabilities are aligned with managing Obsidian Markdown vaults, including search, create, move, rename, delete, and direct note edits; delete and move are sensitive but clearly part of the stated vault-management purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable trusting the yakitrak/yakitrak Homebrew tap and the obsidian-cli tool with access to your Obsidian vault files. Review commands that move or delete notes before running them, especially in work or synced vaults.
llm.findings: [T08] expected: The Homebrew dependency warning is supported by the artifact: obsidian-cli is installed from a mutable third-party tap. This is a real supply-chain consideration, but it is visible in metadata, coherent with the skill purpose, and not evidence of malicious behavior by itself.
